findings: The closed views retain a ribbed hinged enclosure with two side clasps, bottom thumb heads and separate mounting plates. Perspective occlusion can hide the rear plates in a frontal view; oblique and rear views expose them.
The open view exposes the clear factory module, four corner screws, five downward-facing keyed jacks, separate battery/power interfaces, unused analog cover and split bottom cable channel.
The module-hidden view shows the rear battery, two-screw retaining bar and two continuous insulated leads with terminal boots. Their local package, connector dimensions and lengths remain inferred.
The Mini-B mouth shows a real keyed metal opening and five contacts. Its historical GCT dimensional reference does not identify the Onset OEM connector.

The selected Cinch plug is a real seven-part model seated in the third socket. Its transparent body exposes selected contacts; static clearance does not establish latch, electrical or insertion performance.
The rear and mast views preserve the manual's flat-saddle-to-plate direction. Plate holes, U-bolt leg spacing and local fastener geometry remain selected hypotheses.
Surface finish, ribs, internal boards, material appearance and numerous local contours remain authored approximations, not photogrammetry or exact manufacturer CAD.

The inferred mounting plates now use 41 mm height and revised bolt axes. Original positions obstructed the complete selected socket; the separate mast-driver report retains those counterexamples and checks complete-tool space. No source enclosure dimension was changed.
geometry_limits: No inventory, owner acceptance, station installation, seal compression, electrical continuity, structural load or humanoid execution credit. Ordinary-tool static space is covered separately in mast_driver_checks.json.
Sampled door/clasp/plug poses are static inspections, not a manipulation sequence.
Source photographs and drawings are external references and are not redistributed.
